prompt:
Scope (frontend-only): implement client HTTP response parsing, UI rendering, copy/feedback affordances, tests, telemetry/logging handling and documentation so the frontend can display a backend-provided request_id when present in error responses. Do not modify server behavior. Do not assume which specific error types the backend will attach request_id to; detect it by presence and type.

Preserved shared API facts (must be explicitly respected by frontend code):
- Do not change existing API fields: code, message and the HTTP status code must remain unchanged and continue to be displayed/used exactly as before.
- request_id will be added by the backend inside the error object for two specific server error cases. The frontend must not assume which ones; detect presence by inspecting the response body.
- request_id is a backend-generated opaque non-empty string. It must not contain credentials or user-provided input. Treat it as opaque; do not attempt to parse or extract data from it.
- Success (2xx) responses and other non-targeted errors will not include request_id; the frontend must not expect it in normal success flows.

Implementation requirements (step-by-step):
1) Response parsing and validation
  - On every HTTP response with a non-2xx status, parse the response body as JSON if Content-Type is application/json; handle parse failures gracefully (do not throw uncaught exceptions).
  - If parsedBody.error exists and parsedBody.error.request_id exists, validate that typeof request_id === 'string' and request_id.trim().length > 0. Only then treat it as present. If missing, empty, or not a string, treat as absent.
  - Do not mutate or remove existing fields code, message, or status; continue to surface them exactly as before.

2) UI behavior
  - In any error UI (global error banner, API error modals, inline error blocks), if a valid request_id is present per validation above, display it under a small label such as "Request ID:" followed by the opaque string.
  - Place the request_id display close to the existing error message so users/support can copy it when reporting (but do not replace the message or status code).
  - Provide a copy-to-clipboard affordance next to the request_id (accessible button with aria-label). On copy success show a transient confirmation (e.g., tooltip or toast).
  - Make the request_id text selectable and readable; do not hyperlink it or embed it in URLs.
  - Accessibility: ensure the label and copy control are keyboard-focusable and have appropriate aria attributes. Screen readers should be able to read the label and the value.

3) Security and data-handling rules
  - Always escape request_id before inserting into the DOM to prevent XSS. Treat it as untrusted text and render only as text content, never as HTML.
  - Do not append request_id to GET query strings, fragment identifiers, or any URL that could be cached or logged by third parties.
  - Do not include request_id in client-side URLs or route state that might be persisted publicly (e.g., in server logs or bookmarked URLs).
  - Do not derive or infer any credentials, PII, or other secrets from request_id; it is opaque.
  - If storing request_id temporarily in application state for the purpose of user reporting, store it only in memory or encrypted short-lived storage. Avoid long-term persistent storage unless product/privacy policy allows and documents retention.

4) Logging, diagnostics and telemetry
  - When sending client-side diagnostic events to internal error tracking (Sentry, etc.), attach request_id as a discrete metadata field (e.g., event.extra.request_id = '...') rather than concatenating into message text. This preserves the unchanged message/code fields in logs.
  - Do not include request_id in analytics events that are publicly aggregated or shared unless privacy policy and backend support it. If included, ensure it is sent only to internal support channels and documented.
  - Avoid console.log(request_id) in production builds; use structured internal logging that can be restricted by environment/role.

5) Feedback/reporting UX
  - Add a visible option in error dialogs: "Copy Request ID to report" or "Include Request ID when contacting support". If the product currently has a bug-report form, prefill a read-only field with the request_id and let the user include it when sending the report.
  - Do not automatically send request_id to third-party services without confirmation and documented consent. If sending it as part of an automated feedback mechanism, include it as a separate field named request_id in the existing feedback payload (do not alter existing required feedback fields). Coordinate with backend/support teams on any acceptance schema — but do not invent backend fields here.

6) Backward compatibility and fallback
  - If request_id is absent, UI must continue to behave as before; show existing error message and controls. Do not degrade previous UX.
  - If response body is not valid JSON or lacks an error object, gracefully display the generic error message and do not crash.

7) Tests and QA
  - Unit tests: parsing logic must be covered for these cases: missing body, invalid JSON, error without request_id, error with empty or non-string request_id, error with valid request_id. Verify validation logic rejects invalid forms and accepts only non-empty strings.
  - Component/UI tests: verify request_id is displayed only when valid, copy button works and copies exact string, accessibility labels exist, and no HTML injection is possible.
  - End-to-end tests: simulate server responses (non-2xx) that include a valid request_id in the error object and verify the full UX: display, copy, and feedback prefill.

8) Documentation
  - Update frontend API/observer docs to state: "If a server error includes error.request_id (non-empty string), the client will display it and provide copy/report affordances. The fields code, message and HTTP status are unchanged." Include a note: "request_id is backend-generated and opaque; do not treat as secret or user input."

9) Implementation checklist for engineers
  - [ ] Add response parsing helper that extracts validated request_id from error object.
  - [ ] Update error UI components to render request_id when present (with copy control and accessibility attributes).
  - [ ] Ensure all DOM insertion is text-only (no innerHTML with untrusted content).
  - [ ] Add telemetry/logging hook to attach request_id as metadata to internal error events (opt-in by environment).
  - [ ] Add unit, component and E2E tests described above.
  - [ ] Update docs and notify support/QA that front-end will display backend-provided request_id and how to capture it during user reports.

Notes and constraints reminder (do not violate):
- The frontend must not alter or rely on changes to code, message, or HTTP status code — continue to use them unchanged.
- Do not assume which two server error types will include request_id; detect presence dynamically.
- request_id will not include credentials or user input; do not attempt to extract secrets or PII from it.
- Success responses and unrelated errors will not include request_id — the client must not present it in those cases.

Deliverables: updated client parsing/helper module, updated error UI component, unit + integration + E2E tests, updated docs and a small QA checklist for support to verify request_id display and copy behavior.
